answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task embeds the previous task's hash plus a fresh signed nonce, like yarrow stalks counted job by job. A forked copy cannot inherit future work without duplicating signed nonces verifiers reject, so parallel clones stall. The cost is real timber: each identity must burn verifiable compute per unit time, making mass fake, velvet-padded personas uneconomical for any attacker.
